name: Brain Scan (VST3)
description: A free Windows VST3 synth that stores no waveforms. A specimen is a VOLUME - a scalar field filling a cube, exactly the kind of number a scanner records - and a scan line is a curve through it: one cycle of the sound is the field read along that curve. Bend the curve and the timbre changes because the curve is now somewhere else in the body; a closed loop has no edge and sounds soft, an open segment jumps once per cycle and sounds bright, a corner is a kink at a fixed phase, WARP reads the same shape unevenly. The filter's cutoff and the modulator are the same mechanism read slower - two more curves - and one SCAN control blends the GEOMETRY of two anchor lines before anything is read, so halfway between two sounds is tissue neither of them has visited. Fifteen specimens, 128 texels across: nine phantoms built from formulas (six for ordinary useful waveforms, three made of edges and spikes) and six bodies in Hounsfield units - a head, the same head as bare skull, a chest with ribs and lungs, three vertebrae, a thigh, a jaw with teeth - with a radiographer's window presets with skull, cortical folds, a fissure and ventricles. Lines are drawn on a tomography slice that you drive through the body, and watched in a ray-marched gantry where they glow inside the tissue until the density closes over them. IMPORT reads a real volume off disk and uses it instead of the fifteen - a NIfTI file, a folder of DICOM slices or a stack of images - resampled in millimetres so an anisotropic scan is not squashed, area-averaged so decimation does not alias, and windowed by percentile so one surgical clip cannot crush the tissue; with a CT loaded, WINDOW and LEVEL are literally a radiographer's window width and level in Hounsfield units. The read has its own controls - GRAIN picks the kernel, smoothed or texel by texel; CONTRAST is a CT window applied to the sound, saturating the read toward a square; FOLD folds it back past the edges; a 2ND HEAD reads the same line at a ratio of the note for real inharmonic partials; lines can be split into two segments, flattened, reverted and undone, and dragged on the gantry - all anti-aliased. The filter has circuits: beside the state-variable filter, Black Rider's GROWL, SCREAM and LADDER, each as lowpass or highpass, SCREAM and LADDER singing in tune at full resonance. The Brokild World FX rack and five macros. Every claim measured: two benches, 174 checks.
note: Windows VST3 - build 260905.2 - free download - 15 specimens (nine phantoms, six bodies in HU) plus your own volume (NIfTI, DICOM or an image stack) - hints on every control - 18-page manual.
